name: Southern Cornbread Dressing With Oysters and Sausage

cookwares.name: 9- by 13-inch rectangular baking dish (or 10- by 14-inch oval dish)
stiff wire whisk or potato masher

ingredients.name: southern-style unsweetened cornbread, cut into 3/4-inch dice
unsalted butter, plus more for greasing dish
sweet Italian sausage, removed from casing
raw oysters and their liquor, oysters chopped

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven racks to lower-middle and upper-middle positions. Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F). Spread cornbread evenly over 2 rimmed baking sheets. Stagger sheets on oven racks and bake until lightly toasted, about 10 minutes. Remove from oven and allow to cool, about 15 minutes.

While bread is cooling: In a large Dutch oven, melt butter over medium-high heat until foaming subsides, about 2 minutes, without allowing butter to brown. Add sausage and, using a stiff whisk or potato mashers, break up into fine pieces (largest pieces should be no bigger than 0.5 cm). Cook, stirring frequently, until only a few bits of pink remain, about 8 minutes. Add onion, celery, fennel, garlic, and thyme and cook, stirring frequently, until vegetables are softened, about 10 minutes. Remove from heat and add half of chicken stock.

Whisk remaining chicken stock, eggs, tarragon, and 3 tablespoons of parsley in a medium bowl until homogeneous. Stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, slowly pour egg mixture into sausage mixture. Add cornbread cubes, oysters, and oyster liquor and fold gently until evenly mixed. Season lightly with salt and pepper (1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon pepper). Transfer dressing to a buttered 9- by 33-cm rectangular baking dish or 10- by 36-cm oval dish.

Adjust oven rack to center of oven and preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Uncover dressing and bake until an instant-read thermometer reads 66°C (150°F) when inserted into center of dish and dressing is crisped on top, about 45 minutes. Remove from oven, let cool for 15 minutes, sprinkle with remaining 1 tablespoon of parsley, and serve.

description: Adding oysters to Thanksgiving stuffing may sound like an odd choice, but it's a practice with a long history and delicious results. Here, raw chopped oysters are mixed with toasted unsweetened cornbread, sausage, and aromatic vegetables and herbs. The oysters add a wonderful savory flavor and subtle brininess.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 hr 35 min.

Optional substitutions: homemade chicken stock → low-sodium broth

Make-ahead and storage: The dressing can be prepared through step 3, covered with aluminum foil, and refrigerated for up to 2 days in advance or wrapped tightly in plastic wrap and frozen for up to 6 months. If cooking from frozen, bake from frozen for full amount of time.
The dressing can be baked and, once cooled, wrapped tightly in plastic wrap for up to 6 months. Bake in a 350ºF (175ºC) oven until warmed through.
author: Daniel Gritzer
